### What I did

- The default ingest path loaded 50 functions and \`program.check({ count: 1 })\` checked only \`chessSearch\` and \`chessPerft\`, with one successful case apiece. The frames use the caller's buffer, so tape ingest for Typed frame arrays was unnecessary.

- \`tools/reference-check.mjs\` loops over every project even with an id argument. The project runner uses the same reference compiler with the exact assembled source and scopes all generated checks to this project.

The same probe confirmed \`SearchState\` byte offsets and opening perft depth one (20).

# Chess search

Ported from \`apps/typed/chess/\` in ds-js-os at revision
\`b19062b29fe4fb6b02863e92510501dc5c4bc9b3\`. The board is a caller-supplied
u16 buffer with eight ranks at stride 16, starting at rank 8. The first eight
cells of each rank hold files a–h. Cells 128–134 store side to move, castling
rights, the en passant square, both king squares, and both clocks.

- \`chessPerft(board, depth)\` takes a 2,048-cell legal position buffer and
  depth 0–3. It counts legal move paths of exactly that depth and returns 1
  at depth zero.
- \`chessSearch(board, state, depth, budget, advanced)\` takes a 9,216-cell
  legal position buffer, a fresh zeroed \`SearchState\`, depth 1–3, a positive
  node budget, and an advanced-evaluation flag. It runs iterative-deepening
  alpha-beta and returns a packed move, or zero at a terminal position.
  On budget exhaustion it returns the last completed iteration's move or
  the first legal move if the search completed no iteration. The state
  records the score, visited nodes, and completed depth.

Both entries restore cells 0–134 and use the remaining cells as scratch.
Packed moves use \`4096 * promotion + 64 * fromDense + toDense\`, with dense
square zero at a8 and promotion codes 1–4 for queen, rook, bishop, and knight.

Run **explore** in the workbench Scripts view to check \`speed\` on a fresh
